texts.preamble: Moniesh Enterprises vs Food Safety And Standards Authority Of ... on 4 February, 2015 Author: A.Muhamed Mustaque Bench: A.Muhamed Mustaque In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice A.Muhamed Mustaque Tuesday,The 12Th Day Of May 2015/22Nd Vaisakha, 1937 WP(C).No. 10853 of 2015 (F) ---------------------------- Petitioner: ------------------- Moniesh Enterprises, Ist Floor, 1-A, Rondala Govindan Street, Shevapet, Salem, Tamil Nadu, India - 636 002, Represented By Co-Parcaner Mr.Moniesh. By Advs.Sri.Mathews K.Uthuppachan Sri.Terry V.James Respondent(S): -------------------------- 1. Food Safety And Standards Authority Of India, (Ministry Of Health And Family Welfare) Fda Bhavan, Kotla Road, New Delhi - 110002. Represented By The Director. 2. The Authorised Officer, Cochin Sea Port And Air Port, Food Safety And Standards Authority Of India, (Ministry Of Health And Family Welfare) Ist Floor, Marine Building, North End, Moniesh Enterprises vs Food Safety And Standards Authority Of ... on 4 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182653402/ 1 Willingdon Island, Kochi - 682 009. R1 By Sri.N.Nagaresh, As G R2 By Advs. Sri.Mehmood Pracha Sri.Paul Jacob This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Been Finally Heard On 12-05-2015, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: mbr/ WP(C).No. 10853 of 2015 (F) --------------------------------------- Appendix Petitioner(S)' Exhibits: ------------------------------------- Ext.P-1: True Copy Of Packing List.
texts.facts: The imported goods have been detained. Based on the direction of this Court, the sample of imported goods has been send for lab analysis. The report has been received in a sealed cover. On going through the lab report, it is seen that the petitioners goods are in conformity to the standards and there is no impurity or contamination.
texts.arguments: 2. However, the learned Standing counsel for the respondent points out that, in view of the defects in terms of Section 23 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2011 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act' for short), the petitioner's imported goods cannot be released. 3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the above defects are curable defects.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 2.
